title: 5 Best Markdown to HTML Converters in 2026 (Free & Paid)
description: Compare the top Markdown to HTML converters. Free online tools, APIs, and libraries ranked by features, pricing, and ease of use.

sections.heading: Why You Need a Markdown to HTML Converter
sections.content:
Markdown is the lingua franca of developers, technical writers, and content creators. It's used in:

- GitHub READMEs and documentation
- Static site generators (Jekyll, Hugo, Gatsby)
- Note-taking apps (Obsidian, Notion)
- Blogging platforms

But to publish Markdown on the web, you need HTML. While you could write HTML directly, Markdown is 3-4x faster to write and easier to maintain. A good converter bridges this gap — turning your clean Markdown into semantic HTML without touching a tag.

We tested 15+ tools and ranked the top 5 based on conversion quality, features, privacy, and value.

sections.heading: 1. MarkdownMagic (Best Overall)
sections.content:
MarkdownMagic tops our list for its combination of simplicity, privacy, and features.

**What makes it #1:**
- Zero-signup free tier (10 conversions/day)
- Completely browser-based (data never leaves your device)
- Bidirectional: Markdown to HTML AND HTML to Markdown
- Clean, semantic HTML output
- REST API for developers
- Handles all standard Markdown including tables and code blocks

**Pricing:** Free (10/day) or $9/month Pro for unlimited + API

**Best for:** Developers, content creators, and privacy-conscious users who want a fast, reliable tool without account creation.

sections.heading: 2. markdowntohtml.com (Simplest Option)
sections.content:
A straightforward, no-frills converter that does one thing well.

**Pros:**
- Extremely simple interface
- Instant conversion
- No registration required
- Completely free

**Cons:**
- No API access
- No bidirectional conversion
- No code block syntax highlighting
- Limited to small documents

**Pricing:** 100% free

**Best for:** Quick, one-off conversions where you don't need advanced features or API access.

sections.heading: 3. marked (Best for Developers)
sections.content:
For developers building their own applications, marked is the industry-standard JavaScript library.

**Pros:**
- Runs in browser and Node.js
- Highly customizable
- GitHub Flavored Markdown support
- Active development (40k+ GitHub stars)
- Extensive plugin ecosystem

**Cons:**
- Requires coding knowledge
- Need to build your own UI
- No hosted service included

**Pricing:** Free (open source)

**Best for:** Developers integrating Markdown conversion into their own applications or websites.

sections.heading: 4. CodeBeautify (Best for Batch Processing)
sections.content:
CodeBeautify offers a suite of developer tools including Markdown to HTML conversion.

**Pros:**
- Supports multiple formats beyond Markdown
- File upload option (not just paste)
- Additional formatting tools
- No account required

**Cons:**
- Ad-supported interface
- No API
- Mixed quality on complex Markdown
- Privacy concerns (server-side processing)

**Pricing:** Free with ads

**Best for:** Users who need occasional conversions and don't mind a cluttered interface.

sections.heading: 5. Pandoc (Most Powerful)
sections.content:
The Swiss Army knife of document conversion. Pandoc handles Markdown to HTML plus 50+ other formats.

**Pros:**
- Command-line power
- Converts between virtually any format
- Template system for custom output
- Handles complex documents
- Free and open source

**Cons:**
- Steep learning curve
- Command-line only (no GUI)
- Overkill for simple conversions
- Local installation required

**Pricing:** Free

**Best for:** Power users and technical writers who need advanced conversion features and don't mind the command line.
